messages:
Anya: OK team — we're prioritizing the 'adaptive batching' initiative for Q2 to cut token spend for sync chat customers. I need alignment on what runtime/infra/security resourcing and sequencing looks like. Who can outline constraints and minimal safe scope?
Mike: From runtime POV: core work is adaptive batching scheduler + KV cache affinity. Rough estimate: 2 senior runtime engineers for ~8w, plus a part-time perf lead. Risk: kernel changes could impact latency SLOs.
Devon: Infra: we'll need a staging GPU pool with slightly different instance types to test batching under load. Ops estimate: 3 weeks to provision + infra automation for autoscaling policies. Also need quota reserved for canary.
Sara: Security: surface-level ask — we need threat model updated for request routing + KV cache persistence. If customer data touches caching layer we need KMS integration and audit hooks. Timeline: 2 weeks for initial review, 4–6 weeks for remediation if we need HSM or stricter controls.
Anya: Good. Can we run some non-customer experiments first to prove perf characteristics? That would reduce security scope initially.
Mike: Yes — we can run synthetic traffic in staging without customer data. That lets us validate batch heuristics and latency impact.
Ken: As eng manager, can we get a timeline that shows blockers? I want to negotiate scope with PM org — we might phase rollout: internal-only -> beta customers -> GA.
Priya: SRE flag: rolling deploy and observability changes required. We need token-level cost breakdown per route and new tracing to debug batching-induced tail latencies. Plan: 2 SREs for 3 weeks to add tracing + dashboards.
Anya: Launch criteria proposal: 1) <=5% median latency regression, 2) >=15% token-cost reduction on target workloads, 3) observability + rollback in place, 4) security sign-off or approved mitigation plan. Thoughts?
Mike: Fine but add: no customer-facing error rate increase during canary (strict 99.9% success).
Devon: Infra dependency: reserve 10 GPUs for canary week and ability to scale +50% during peak. If procurement needed, that pushes schedule by 2–3 weeks.
Sara: If caching remains ephemeral and doesn't store PHI, we can parallelize security review. If customers like Acme Health require data-at-rest guarantees, that will require KMS/HSM and could slip GA. Flagging that now.
Anya: Ok — let's put together a tight phased plan. Action items: 1) Mike + Ken: deliver runtime spike + perf numbers by 1719920000 (in 6 days). 2) Devon: confirm canary capacity timeline by 1719950000 (in 3 business days). 3) Sara: initial threat model by 1719925000. 4) Priya: tracing/dashboard spec by 1719930000. I'll consolidate and run with PM leads.
Ken: I'll allocate 2 runtime engineers (Eve + Omar) and one perf engineer (part-time). If infra can't hit dates we reduce scope to server-side batching only (no cross-model caching).
Mike: Noted. Will scope the spike to both server batching and a tiny KV-affinity proof that doesn't persist across requests.
Anya: Thanks. If anyone wants to be cc'd on the consolidated plan ping me. I'll schedule a 30min sync next Tue to lock decision. :calendar: @devon @sara @mike
infra-bot: New ticket created: INF-4231 "Adaptive batching canary capacity" assigned to Devon, due 1719950000.
Priya: One more thing — add an SLO rollback playbook for batching gone-wrong (scripts to disable batching per route). I'll draft it after dashboards are spec'd.
Anya: Great — looks like we have initial alignment. I'll post the consolidated plan after I get the spike numbers. :white_check_mark:
